summary: @servicetitan/examples ships a preinstall Bun-runtime dropper that executes an obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"` in package.json, causing setup.mjs to run automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs uses hex-name identifier obfuscation (e.g. `_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`) to hide a fetch-and-execute chain: it downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/...zip`, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and immediately invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js])` against a bundled sibling file. `math_init.js` is a 727 KB Bun-compiled artifact (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) whose contents are hidden behind a rotated numeric string-array cipher with decoder functions `hc1jfK9`/`WV8StW`, so its behavior cannot be inspected by Node-based tooling. Fetching an alternate JavaScript runtime at install time specifically to execute an obfuscated bundle Node cannot parse is a supply-chain attack pattern, not a legitimate build step. The package is additionally published under the `@servicetitan/*` scope with 17 `@servicetitan/*` dependencies, empty description, and no author/repository fields, presenting itself as an official ServiceTitan examples package to encourage unscrutinized installs.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
